title: Delight of Parvati
translation: His mind rejoices in the graceful play of the daughter of the king of mountains (Parvati), which lights up every direction. The stream of his merciful glances holds back even the hardest misfortunes. May my mind find joy in that Digambara, clothed only by the directions.
translation_hi: जिनका मन पर्वतराज की पुत्री पार्वती की लीलाओं से, जो सब दिशाओं को प्रकाशित करती हैं, आनंदित रहता है, और जिनकी कृपा दृष्टि की धारा कठिन से कठिन विपत्तियों को रोक देती है, उन दिगंबर शिव में मेरा मन आनंद पाए।

words.note: kripa = mercy (Hindi कृपा); kataksha = sidelong glance.
Same √rudh as the trapped bee (Lilavati verse 3) and प्रतिरोध (resistance).
durdhara (hard to bear) + apad (calamity, Hindi आपदा).
dik (directions) + ambara (clothes). क् → ग् before a vowel.
-अः → -ओ before a voiced sound: मनो विनोदम्.

words.meaning: may it go, may it reach

grammar: Imperative of √i 'go': विनोदम् एतु 'may it go to joy', meaning 'may it find joy'. A tiny verb: एति (goes), एतु (may it go).
Consonant sandhi: दिक् + अम्बर → दिगम्बर. A hard consonant softens before a vowel, like वेगात् → वेगाद् in the bamboo verse.
Root √rudh: निरुद्ध 'blocked'. One root gives निरुद्ध (blocked), प्रतिरोध (resistance) and अवरोध (obstruction).
